segments.text: Bhaiya's Teachings
Session 108 — The Thir d Eye's Thir d Batch: Strict Rules, the Second-Charan Japa Method, the Four Adhishthatri Devtas, Parallel-Universe Rules, and the Full MantraDimension Mapping
Ash aeiy n n · Th ird Ey e Sp ecial Batch — Th ird Co h o rt, 1 1 -Day Sad h n a
Part I: Kn o wled g e Base  •  Part II: Q&A Pairs
Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 108, English)
The Third Eye's Third Batch Begins: Strict Rules, the Second-Charan Japa Method, and Why Bhagwan Ram Is So Strict

This session opens a new cohort — explicitly described as the thir d batch of the Thir d Eye pr ogram — with its own fr esh welcome, its own framing of heightened seriousness and strictness, a detailed walkthr ough of the 1 1-day sadhna's practical rules and the second-charan (second-stage) japa method, an extensive live Q&A round on pr ocedural questions, and a closing teaching on why Bhagwan Ram is strict compar ed to Hanuman ji's gentleness. It closes with its own sankalp and send-off chant.
Part A — Opening the Third Batch

1. A fresh welcome to a new , mor e advanced batch: The speaker opens with a formal welcome, noting that mentors have "pushed forward" these particular devotees specifically so that work can begin on their drishti — signaling that this cohort is understood to already have some prior grounding.

2. Personal, dir ect checking: The speaker states he will personally check everyone's japa himself, not merely take devotees' own word for how much practice they have done — and that any guidance he gives will come from what Baba instructs him, not his own preference.

3. Zero tolerance for car elessness in this batch: The speaker states plainly that no mistakes or excuses will be tolerated in this Third Eye track, and that time will not be wasted on unproductive discussion of why something isn't being done.
4. No "ifs, ands, or buts": Devotees are told that if they cannot commit fully , they should either leave now or wait for a future batch — there is no room for conditional participation this time.

5. An 1 1-day sankalp, taken immediately: Devotees who choose to continue can message the speaker directly in the admin section, and their sankalp for the next 1 1 days of training will be taken on the spot; anyone who will be busy during this window should leave before the sankalp is taken.

6. A warning about wasting invoked shakti: Per this teaching, the shakti (spiritual power) invoked and sent to stand with each devotee day and night deserves respect through consistent ef fort — neglecting that ef fort after such power has been dedicated is described as understandably provoking frustration from those overseeing the process.
Part B — Why This Batch Is Held to a Higher Standard

1. Higher expectations because of what devotees alr eady know: Per this teaching, this particular batch is held to unusually high standards specifically because these devotees already understand how Ashaeiynn and its shakti function, unlike newer devotees who are still being introduced to the basics.

2. No going back: The speaker states that turning back now , after devotees have already opened their chakras, of fered their body's elements, and received saints' dedicated time, would be considered deeply unworthy — and states he will not allow it to happen without consequence.

3. The "sword" analogy for this batch's added power: Per this teaching, devotees previously worked with something comparatively mild (described as "a light rod"); in this batch, they are being handed something far more powerful and correspondingly more dangerous (described as "a sword") — those who handle it carefully benefit, and those who mishandle it can be hurt, so the speaker frames himself as staying close to help devotees handle it safely , while devotees themselves must learn to hold and use it responsibly .

4. A shift in the character of the shakti being sent: Per this teaching, the gentler , more for giving ener gies devotees have relied on until now will be replaced in this batch by comparatively fiercer ("ugra") ener gies — not because devotees did anything wrong, but because this is simply the next stage of the process.

5. Rules increase as r esponsibility incr eases: Per this teaching, as a devotee draws closer to the divine, more rules and required sankalp-discipline accompany that closeness — described as the natural cost ("protocol") of claiming a closer relationship with that power , not an arbitrary imposition.
Part C — Practical Rules for the 1 1-Day Sadhna
1. A guru/Baba photo as the sadhna's visual anchor: Devotees will be sent a photo of the guru to print or keep on their phone, to be placed in front of a lit diya during sadhna.

2. Tilak and offerings: Devotees apply tilak by their own hand, followed by rice; sandalwood, perfume (itar), or flowers may optionally be added — but tilak and rice specifically are described as necessary .
3. The four -element combination: Per this teaching, the practitioner's own body , the tilak, the rice, and the earth beneath together form a necessary four -part combination for this sadhna.

4. Gazing at the guru's eyes while chanting: Devotees are told to look into the eyes of the guru's photo while chanting — not in a fixed, unblinking (tratak-style) stare, but naturally: looking at the eyes when their own eyes are open, closing their eyes to continue the mental repetition, and returning their gaze to the eyes when they reopen them.

5. A dedicated, undisturbed, self-cleaned sadhna space: The chosen sadhna spot should not be occupied by anyone else, and devotees are told to personally clean the space themselves rather than delegating it to household help — described as a matter of the devotee's own ef fort and respect for the space, not a strict prohibition on staf f entering the room generally .

6. Sleeping on the gr ound: Devotees are asked to sleep on the ground for the 1 1 days (a mattress placed on the floor is permitted) — explained as allowing visiting saints to touch a sleeping devotee more easily than if they were sleeping raised above the ground.
7. Eating and drinking r estriction: After 6:00 p.m., only warm water should be consumed — no food.

8. An optional pairing with Siya tattva sadhna: For devotees already practicing Siya tattva sadhna, continuing it is described as especially beneficial during this batch, since it keeps the practitioner's body elements already bound in a compatible way and reinforces the same character this sadhna requires — described as "two tar gets with one arrow ." Devotees already doing an allday version of this practice were told the fixed 4-hour japa here fulfills that day's practice; a full day's continuous chanting is not additionally required.

9. A four -hour minimum, seated only: Devotees must complete at least four hours of this sadhna's japa daily , seated properly (on an asan or however comfortable, cross-legged or with legs extended as needed) — walking or otherwise moving during this
specific japa does not count toward the four hours. More than four hours is permitted only if done seated in the same posture.

10. Splitting the four hours, and physical effects to expect: Devotees may split the four hours into blocks (for example, one or two hours at a time) with short breaks (including water breaks) in between. Per this teaching, sustained second-charan japa at this level can cause a heavy , "splitting" sensation in the head, bodily heaviness, or a feeling of pressure from multiple directions — devotees were told not to be alarmed by this, and were cautioned specifically not to continue any additional japa beyond this sadhna during the 1 1 days, since doing so risks a persistent headache.

1 1. Preferring night-time practice: The speaker recommends devotees do this sadhna at night rather than during the day , in a space where they will not disturb others and will not be disturbed, and suggests sleeping immediately adjacent to that same spot afterward.

12. Expect significant bodily sensations, without alarm: Skipping food after 6 p.m. may itself make sleep dif ficult and produce sensations resembling heat, illness, or even fever; devotees were told these are expected "tremendous changes" in the body during this process and not cause for panic.
Part D — The Second-Charan Japa Method, Explained

1. The cor e method: Devotees gaze at the guru's photo's eyes while mentally repeating "Ram Ram Ram..." continuously , keeping their focus entirely on this internal repetition; when their mind drifts from center , they should close their eyes, refocus on the repetition, and reopen their eyes to return their gaze to the photo.

2. A postur e of humble r equest, not entitlement: Devotees were told nothing is gained through ego or self-assertion; instead, they should of fer sincere prayer/entreaty (illustrated with the lines "prabhu nath karahu so bhaanti, sab taj bhajahu karo din raati" and "mo bhoras hanumant nabo, hari kripa binu milahin nahi santa" — meaning grace of this kind comes only through Hanuman ji's mediated grace, not by claim).

3. A gratitude framework — five r easons this sadhna has been given: Devotees were told to first thank Baba for the sadhna itself, then to recognize five underlying reasons they have received it: (1) the devotion, power , and ef fort of those in the guru lineage who directed them here; (2) the devotee's own prior tapasya; (3) the required approval of the saints — no sadhna is received without their consent; (4) the devotee's own past-life powers, which are understood to actively draw a devotee back toward this kind of practice; and (5) guru bal (the guru's own spiritual strength) and Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace.

4. A caution against interpr eting visions independently: Per this teaching, drishti that is not yet meant to open should not be forced open by the devotee, since doing so causes confusion; devotees were warned that once drishti opens, illusions are possible — even a vision that appears to show the guru or Hanuman ji himself striking the devotee — and were told never to assume such a vision's meaning on their own, but instead to ask directly , "please connect with me and guide me," rather than jumping to a personal interpretation.
Part E — Daily Personal Checking and Contact

1. Daily one-on-one checking begins the next day: Starting the day after this session, the speaker will personally check each devotee individually — their japa, mantra ener gy , hawan needs, doshas, past-life powers, and dimensional progress — every day at a fixed time.

2. Open, direct contact: Devotees may message or call the speaker directly at any time, including late at night, and were told replies would come even then — with the caveat that this channel is for reporting genuine problems (via voice note to the admin number), not for announcing an intent to quit partway through.
Part F — The Speaker's Own First Experience of This Level of Sadhna

1. Frightening early visions, not fanciful ones: The speaker recounts that when Baba first guided him through this style of sadhna, his very first sitting showed him disturbing, alien-feeling realms rather than anything pleasant, leaving him shaken.
2. Persisting despite fear: He describes returning to sit again despite the disturbing first experience, after which the visions gradually began revealing more of an underlying reality day by day .

3. Being shown "the formation of the Earth": The speaker recounts that in this way , Baba eventually taught him about the formation of the Earth in a single class — an experience he says shook him profoundly , and one he has still only received once.

4. A caution drawn fr om other devotees losing faith afterward: The speaker recounts that following that particular teaching, some devotees who lost faith in Baba afterward came under attack, and had to be brought back and have their sankalp/shakti reinvoked — of fered as a caution to maintain faith and persistence even after encountering unsettling experiences in this practice.
Part G — Live Pr ocedural Q&A Round

1. Overview: As with prior sessions, an extended live Q&A round followed the formal teaching, covering practical questions about how to apply these rules; the exchanges are summarized here by topic (this session's checking-round content did not include enough distinct, quotable back-and-forth to warrant a separate curated Hinglish conversation section).

2. Continuing existing pr ofessional r eadings: A devotee who does astrology readings for work was told she may continue if it is her livelihood, though the speaker suggested pausing non-essential readings during the 1 1 days if possible.
3. Displaying the guru's photo: Devotees were told the manner of displaying the sent photo (printing, laminating, building a small shrine, placement) is entirely up to their own preference.
4. When the daily sankalp/japa clock starts: Japa for the day begins once that day's sankalp has been taken (of fered around a fixed daily time), not from an earlier point in the day .

5. A devotee's physical r esponse during this explanation: One devotee described a racing heartbeat and a hot sensation in her head simply while listening to the day's teaching; this was explained as a natural rise in ener gy , not a cause for concern.

6. Pausing other personal rituals: Devotees who perform other regular household rituals (for example, water or oil of ferings) not connected to Ashaeiynn were told they may pause these for the 1 1 days if they choose, while family kul devata diyas may continue as usual in every case.
7. Optional additional diyas: Lighting additional diyas (for example, eleven) is permitted if a devotee wishes, but the sadhna itself should be performed only once per day .

8. Practicing during work hours: Devotees who cannot attend live sessions due to work were told they may listen in quietly during breaks and are not required to be continuously present, as long as they complete their own japa separately .

9. Accommodating travel or unavailability: A devotee unable to attend the final two days of the 1 1-day window was told this was not a problem and that arrangements (darshan) would be adjusted accordingly .
10. No impact fr om menstruation: A devotee asked whether her monthly cycle would create any dif ficulty during these 1 1 days; she was told plainly that it would cause no dif ficulty at all.
1 1. Seated postur e is required: Japa must be performed seated on an asan for the entire four hours (or however long a devotee chooses beyond the minimum), not while walking or moving.

12. No r estriction on gr ooming: Devotees asked whether they could shave, cut hair , or otherwise groom themselves during the 1 1 days; they were told this was entirely permitted with no restriction.
Part H — Closing Teaching: Why Bhagwan Ram Is So Strict

1. Contrasting Ram's strictness with Hanuman ji's gentleness: Per this teaching, Hanuman ji Maharaj is experienced as gentle and for giving, while Bhagwan Ram — described as maryada purushottam (the ideal upholder of righteous conduct) — is very strict and, per this teaching, would act immediately against wrongdoing on his guru's instruction regardless of who was involved.

2. Why gr eater responsibility r equires gr eater strictness: Per this teaching, the more responsibility a position carries, the stricter its holder must be to maintain the power entrusted to that position — illustrated by contrasting Ram (holder of ultimate power , and thus very strict) with Hanuman ji (who wields that power on Ram's behalf, and can therefore be gentler).

3. Ram's eighteen siddhis: Per this teaching, a devotee who genuinely practices sadhna dedicated to Bhagwan Ram has eighteen siddhis (spiritual attainments) made available to them — described as unmatched by any other tattva in the world, contrasted with Krishna's traditionally cited sixteen kalas (arts/attainments).

4. The promised pr otection of Ram's power: Per this teaching, a devotee who genuinely attains this power becomes untouchable by any worldly force, and saints of the naga sect are described as bowing to such a devotee on their toes — of fered as a solemn promise (vachan) within this teaching.

5. Discipline and keeping one's word make sankalp manifest: Per this teaching, if a devotee remains as strict and disciplined with themselves as this practice requires, their own spoken word begins to carry real power and manifest — but only if the devotee actually follows through on what they have committed to; failing to follow through means their stated intentions will not manifest.

6. The closing blessing: The session closes with a blessing that sustained devotion following through on this discipline will bring honor , reputation, and Bhagwan Ram's protection to the devotee, followed by a formal send-of f chant.
Part I — The Four Adhishthatri Devtas, Explained in Depth

1. What "adhishthatri devta" means: Per this teaching, an adhishthatri devta/devi is the presiding deity from which something originates or begins — every person has four such deities governing their subtle body , with kul devata (family/lineage deities) sitting at least eleven levels above these four .

2. The first — the space-element deity: This deity controls a person's space (akash) element, through which all of a person's past-life powers and subtle bodies flow; per this teaching, "winning over" this deity gives access to many of those powers at once, which is why many practitioners specifically focus devotion on this deity .

3. The second — the deity contr olling blood/flow: Per this teaching, this deity is popularly thought of as controlling "the body" generally , but its real domain is blood and blood pressure/flow specifically — described as the true foundation of nearly all bodily function and disease (cancer , heart conditions, or gan health, skin, and cell regeneration are all tied, in this teaching, to blood flow). Devotees at Ashaeiynn with medical drishti are described as perceiving blood flow specifically , distinct from those who perceive bone structure.

4. A contr oversial teaching fr om this deity's tradition: Practitioners devoted to this deity (associated with those who study vata-pitta-kapha and Ayurveda) hold that every element of the body should be allowed to change and regenerate naturally and continuously — extending this to a claim that retaining "veerya" (seed) for long periods causes stagnation, and that physical

intimacy is accordingly necessary for vitality , comparing this to how exercise breaks down and rebuilds stronger muscle tissue. This tradition is said to trace some of its reasoning to Acharya Patanjali's yoga sutras and to the mool bandh kriya. This is explicitly presented as one tradition's own controversial hypothesis and perspective, not as Ashaeiynn's own prescription.

5. The third — the vayu (air/br eath)-element deity: This deity governs the body's air/breath pressure; per this teaching, a person with a very strong vayu element is exceptionally physically powerful ("vayu putra") — the reason, per this teaching, that both Hanuman ji and Bhima are described this way .

6. Two categories of br eath, and what each str engthens: Per this teaching, breath falls into two broad categories — urdhagami (upward-moving) and deer ghagami (outward/extended) — with deer ghagami breath strengthening both the sattvik and tamasik tendencies, while increased urdhagami breath strengthens the rajasik tendency; oxygen intake (not food) is described as the real source of bodily ener gy , with food's role being to supply the ener gy needed to process that oxygen.

7. A strong vayu element without upward r edirection stays "below the waist," metaphorically: Per this teaching, a person with a very strong vayu element who has not redirected that ener gy upward tends to have their focus and awareness centered lower in the body ("apna dimaag ghutno mein"), remaining very physically powerful but not especially perceptive — until that ener gy is redirected upward through meditation, at which point such a person becomes exceptionally intelligent as well as powerful, needing no other deity's help since their own brain begins generating unusual capability directly (described using the "100% brain use" idea).

8. Hanuman ji's own vayu story: Per this teaching, Hanuman ji was originally born with an overwhelmingly vayu-dominant body , with nearly all of that ener gy concentrated below the waist; concerned that this was excessive, sages and his mother Anjana had this lower ener gy bound through spiritual means, leaving him feeling he had lost his power entirely . Anjana then revealed that dhyana (meditation) could redirect this same ener gy upward; through knowledge, meditation, and sustained sadhna, Hanuman ji learned to draw his own vayu ener gy upward into his brain, becoming, per this teaching, "master of masters" — with his body's own pre-established channel (built through this training) allowing the redirected ener gy to be absorbed safely rather than causing harm, unlike (per this teaching) an untrained body such as Bhima's.

9. A distinction fr om typical "astral flight" sadhna: Per this teaching, a common form of "flying" sadhna involves calling upon an external astral hand/force that lifts and then eventually releases the practitioner; Hanuman ji's method, by contrast, is described as using his own brain/ener gy directly rather than relying on an external astral force — a person whose vayu element is already strong and who also redirects that ener gy upward is described as becoming truly extraordinary .

10. The fourth — the earth-element deity: Per this teaching, this deity (described as appearing very still, almost stone-like, seated in a triangular formation, with only the eyes visibly moving) governs a person's earth element — described as the body's magnetic force, meaning the ability to attract and to repel.

1 1. Why physical str ength alone doesn't guarantee charisma: Per this teaching, Maa Anjana secretly taught Hanuman ji that the vayu (air) and prithvi (earth) elements naturally repel one another — meaning a person very strong in vayu (physical power/intelligence) will typically be correspondingly weaker in earth element (personal magnetism/charisma), so their words and presence carry less "weight" with others even if they are individually brilliant or powerful.

12. Why Hanuman ji specifically sought Sita Mata's blessing: Per this teaching, understanding this principle, Hanuman ji deliberately went to Sita Mata — not directly to Bhagwan Ram — asking her blessing and to accept him as her disciple, specifically to acquire the earth-element attractiveness he otherwise lacked; this is presented as evidence of his own deep intelligence in recognizing precisely which element he needed and from whom to seek it, completing him and making him maximally attractive/charismatic across the world once this earth element increased.

13. A practical takeaway — satisfying even two of the four devtas is transformative: Per this teaching, a person does not need to master all four adhishthatri devtas to become exceptional; satisfying even two of the four can make someone remarkable in
their own way (for example, being both highly intelligent via the vayu-element pathway and highly attractive via the earthelement pathway).

14. A practical starting point — understanding one's own constitution: Per this teaching, before pursuing any of these deities, a devotee should first understand their own basic constitution (vata/pitta/kapha-style self-assessment) rather than relying on generic external tests, since this self-understanding shows where a devotee's own natural strengths and deficiencies lie.

15. Different traditions ("cults") have each formed corr ectly ar ound a differ ent one of these deities: Per this teaching, various spiritual traditions and cultures have each historically focused devotion on one of these four adhishthatri devtas, and each such tradition, in its own domain, is described as legitimate and accurate — with a caution not to disparage or work against any of these established traditions.

16. A caution about negative company , and about pitru's possessiveness: Per this teaching, good company matters — someone in a devotee's life who reflexively discourages everything is compared to a pitru's typical possessiveness, since pitru (who per this teaching normally come from the father's lineage, unless the mother's kul devata are the ones actively worshipped in the home) can resist a devotee's growth simply because they cannot bear to see the devotee outgrow them or move beyond their own reach, sometimes manifesting even through the devotee's own living family members' resistance.

17. Why devotees need many people, not just one, ar ound them: Per this teaching, pitru and one's own past-life-connected souls are what actually draw people into a devotee's orbit and sustain a sense of not being alone; a devotee who successfully reduces pitru attachment gains clarity of thought (thinking for themselves, manifesting more easily) but must then rely on their own past-life-connected souls to keep meaningful people close, since — illustrated by the public outpouring of af fection at Arun Jaitley's passing — this kind of drawing power is understood to trace to pitru or past-life soul-connections rather than one's own individual charisma alone.
Part J — Resolving a Contradiction: Hanuman Ji's Dimension and His Pr esence on Earth

1. The appar ent contradiction: A devotee raised an apparent contradiction: an earlier teaching placed Baba (the guru figure, used here as an illustrative stand-in) in the sixth dimension, while tradition holds that Hanuman ji Maharaj is present in an awakened state on this very earth — seemingly two incompatible claims.

2. The resolution — "plane" is one, "dimension" (aayam) differs: Per this teaching, both statements can be true at once because the underlying location (plane) is the same even though the dimensional "layer" dif fers — illustrated by a devotee sitting in earth's ordinary third-dimensional (physical) reality while Baba occupies the same physical location's plane, but stacked at the sixth dimensional layer directly "above" it, much like a dream within a dream occupying the same narrative space at dif ferent depths.

3. What this means practically: Per this teaching, if a devotee could access all six dimensional layers simultaneously at their own physical location, they would perceive Baba directly there, since he is not elsewhere — he is at the same location, just at a dif ferent dimensional depth.

4. Extending the mapping further: Per this teaching, crossing further dimensional layers at that same location would reveal Bhagwan Shiva directly at the tenth dimension, Brahma ji at the eighth dimension, and Vaikuntha at the fourteenth dimension — of fered as the reason these are traditionally described as "everywhere" or requiring no separate journey to reach.

5. A caveat about formal science's own dimensional hypotheses: Per this teaching, quantum physics is said to hypothesize as many as roughly 44 dimensions; this is mentioned only to indicate how many "parallel universes" a person can in principle access, not as a claim this teaching itself adopts as precise fact — the exact number cited varies informally from one telling of this teaching to another .
Part K — How Miracles and Healing Work: Borr owing Fr om One's Own Parallel Universe

1. A guiding example — two childr en with the same illness: Per this teaching, if two children (illustratively named here Piyush and Jivika) have an identical illness, a healer with this kind of siddhi would first check whether the same illness fails to exist in any of the parallel universes reachable by their own power (a small number of universes "above" and "below" their own, depending on how much shakti they personally possess, drawn from sources such as hawan, guru lineage, or their own attained tattvas).

2. When the sear ch succeeds and fails: Per this teaching, if no version of the healthy/cured state can be found in any of the reachable parallel universes for one child (Jivika, in the example), the healer cannot help that child; but if a healthy version is found for the other child (Piyush), the corresponding healthy "tattva" (element/state) can be drawn from that parallel universe and substituted into the child's own body — without disturbing the normal cycle of that reachable parallel universe — producing what looks like an immediate, complete recovery .

3. Why the r emoved illness cannot simply be discarded into another person's universe: Per this teaching, the diseased element that is removed cannot be thrown into someone else's parallel universe (that would be a serious violation, discussed further below); it can only be released into open space, where it eventually cycles back to the same person, sometimes after being bound and delayed for months or years by protective measures, but never permanently eliminated that way — whereas exchanging it directly within one's own reachable parallel universes produces a full, lasting recovery .

4. Why this ability commands r eal r ever ence: Per this teaching, a saint or practitioner who can genuinely do this is described as truly capable of miracles and deserving of the devotion given to them, distinct from lesser feats like naming a color or a detail about someone's personal life.
Part L — Parallel Universe Rules: White Magic, Black Magic, and Why Wrongdoers Aren't Always Caught

1. The cor e rule: Per this teaching, a practitioner may only draw a tattva/element from their own parallel universes — never from someone else's. Deviating from this rule and drawing from another person's parallel universe/dimension is what this teaching calls black magic; drawing legitimately from one's own is called (in this teaching's informal framing) white magic, the kind of exchange devtas themselves use when bestowing a blessing.

2. What happens when someone draws fr om another person's dimension: Per this teaching, doing so makes a practitioner a "defaulter" in the subtle world; a saint with suf ficiently greater dimensional reach who identifies this violation has the standing authority to punish the of fender directly .

3. Why offenders ar en't always caught: Per this teaching, enforcement is inconsistent (compared informally to "rules exist only when the police are present") — a saint only intervenes if and when a wrongdoer happens to fall within that saint's own awareness and reach, not through constant, universal surveillance.

4. The "decoy" mechanism experienced tantriks use to evade consequences: Per this teaching, practitioners who knowingly draw from others' dimensions and expect eventual consequences often pre-arrange multiple unconnected, unaware people (illustratively described as ten to twelve) as "decoy" subtle bodies tied loosely to their own — compared to how some people hold multiple fake identification documents. When a saint eventually catches and curses the of fending practitioner , the resulting misfortune lands on one of these decoy people (who may suf fer greatly or even die) rather than on the practitioner responsible, who walks away unaf fected or even benefits.

5. Why this makes the practice especially harmful and hard to trace: Per this teaching, the decoy people af fected typically have no idea why misfortune has struck them and may wrongly attribute it to their own ancestral (pitru) dosha, when in fact they were never connected to the underlying wrongdoing at all.

6. A student's follow-up — shouldn't mor e powerful saints alr eady know about this loophole?: Per this teaching, saints engaged in deep sadhna are not constantly monitoring for every wrongdoer's scheme; their focus is their own path, compared informally to how someone constructing a building does not personally track every commission an agent quietly siphons of f elsewhere. Per this teaching, in the subtle world, "right and wrong" in a given moment is ef fectively determined by whoever holds greater power at that moment — illustrated by the claim that whatever Bhagwan Krishna did was accepted as right simply because his power was so much greater than anyone contesting it. This is of fered explicitly as a description of how the subtle world is observed to function ("to see the world as it is"), not as a moral endorsement — the speaker is explicit that this is analysis, not an ethics lesson.

7. Does an unknowing decoy incur any fault themselves?: Per this teaching, no dosha attaches to an unknowing, unintentional role in someone else's wrongdoing — of fered alongside the observation that nearly everyone's own astrological chart carries some dosha regardless, which is not by itself evidence of wrongdoing.

8. Does holding multiple decoy subtle bodies itself cr eate a fault for the offending practitioner?: Per this teaching, yes, obviously — described through the saying "a lion is always eventually met by one and a quarter lions" (someone stronger eventually confronts and checks any overreaching wrongdoer) and "the peak of one mountain is the start of another ," meaning no wrongdoer's advantage is considered permanent or beyond eventual correction.

9. The speaker's own personal anecdotes on this topic: The speaker recounts that during the period of his own Mool Tatva videos, his own dimension was once deliberately lowered/attacked, and that he and others identified and "wrapped up" 38 responsible tantriks in response, treating the experience afterward almost lightly in hindsight. He separately recounts encountering extraordinarily advanced saints capable of perceiving even a person's individual breaths, and cautions strongly against ever provoking such beings — recounting an instance of being overheard in what he believed was a private conversation with his own brother , and having to plead that he intended no of fense and bore no connection to the being in question — noting that even in such cases, a powerful being rarely "leaves empty-handed," but that this kind of encounter is simply how practitioners learn.
Part M — A Third Day's Recap, Reminders, and What's Next

1. A firm reminder about following instructions: The speaker reiterates that any devotee who does not follow the given rules cannot be helped further , restating that this batch is held to a stricter standard precisely because these devotees already know how Ashaeiynn and its shakti function.

2. A recap of the batch's early sessions: The speaker recaps that the first day was essentially an orientation, an early day covered the four adhishthatri devtas, and another day covered the electron-proton-neutron/dimension framework used to understand the existence of the earth and of the divine — with the batch about to move on to the "science of mantra."

3. The promise for completing this sadhna eleven times: Per this teaching, completing this 1 1-day sadhna cycle a full eleven times (not merely once) is framed as producing full realization — the ability to perceive past, present, and future about any person on sight, to understand others' thoughts, and to have one's own japa/tapasya manifest immediately .

4.
